$comment: Alias map provisioned into CI runs of council-review.yml.
A runner has no user config, so without this file every alias falls back to
the pinned table in src/utils/curated-models.js (toDefaultAliases) — which
tracks what this package SHIPS, not what the bench should review with.
Read at run time via `gh api` from the BASE ref (never the PR head), because
council-review.yml deliberately never checks out PR code.
Pins are exact ids on purpose: OpenRouter's floating `~vendor/x-latest` ids
carry no canonical target, so a floating pin is invisible in both the
pre-flight table and the spend ledger — you could never tell what reviewed.
Exact pins go stale instead, so alias-pin-drift.yml watches them weekly.
`amicus models --check` does NOT cover these: glm/qwen/kimi are flat CARDLESS
entries with no idPattern, so its audit only asks whether the id still exists.
outputBudget is the per-leg max_tokens reservation for a CI council run. One
shared engine serves the whole run (run.json :: sharedServer.acquired), so the
same number governs Stage 1, its retry, Stage 2 and the chair alike. Unset, the
engine's own 32000 default governs: 4 of the 6 seats lost across the FIVE paid
v4.9.6 council runs died against it with finish 'length' and 0-651 usable
output tokens. A runner never writes model-catalog.json -- nothing on the
`council run` path does -- so buildProviderModels emits {} for every row and
OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX is the ONLY live half of this lever.
Engine ceilings read from /config/providers with the bare {} descriptors amicus
actually registers, opencode-ai 1.18.15, one probe case per process (2026-09-09).
Both catalogue states are recorded because the engine's models.dev fetch is a
RACE against the run's first requests, not a state CI is reliably in:
COLD (bundled catalogue): z-ai/glm-5.3 and qwen/qwen3.8-27b report
limit {context:0, output:0} -- an unknown row, so the budget passes as-is;
deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 65536; google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview 65536;
openai/gpt-5.6-terra 128000.
WARM (after the live fetch lands): qwen3.8-27b 131072,
deepseek-v4-flash-0731 943718; the other three unchanged.
64000 was MEASURED on the wire to land unclamped on all four seats AND the
chair in BOTH states -- it is the largest round value that does.
THE BINDING CEILING IS 65536, AND COLD IT IS SHARED BY TWO ROWS: the chair
(google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview) and deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 -- not by
the chair alone. MEASURED, not inferred: the flag at 100000 reaches the wire as
max_tokens 65536 on the chair (4 of 4 reads) and on deepseek on every COLD read
(4 of 5; the one warm read passed 100000). So a budget above 65536 is silently
clamped on those two while landing in full on glm/qwen/gpt, and the run stops
reserving one number. Raising past 65536 needs a fresh measurement of BOTH
rows, not a reading of the warm deepseek ceiling. tests/ci-council-bench-config.test.js
pins the bound; council-review.yml's pre-flight step fails the run before any
spend on a budget above it, or on one amicus would reject outright (a string, a
zero, a non-number) and silently replace with the 32000 default.
